chunks: 3355 - Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a dhimmī and a slave who are made witnesses to a testimony, then the dhimmī becomes Muslim and the slave is emancipated: is their testimony regarding that to which they had been made witnesses valid?
He said: "Yes, if goodness is known from them after that, their testimony is valid."

key_terms.الذِّمِّيِّ: a non-Muslim living under Islamic protection
key_terms.خَيْرٌ: uprightness or goodness recognized in a person

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a former dhimmī or emancipated slave valid in Islam if they witnessed something before their status changed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the admissibility of testimony initially witnessed by a dhimmī and a slave before their status changed. It indicates that after the dhimmī accepts Islam and the slave is emancipated, their testimony may be accepted if uprightness and goodness become known from them afterward.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3355 - Al-Ala narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim:

He said: I asked Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a dhimmi (non-Muslim under Islamic protection) and a slave who bore witness to a testimony. Then the dhimmi embraced Islam and the slave was emancipated, would their testimony about what they were made witnesses to before be valid?
Imam (as) said: "Yes, if goodness is known from them afterward, their testimony is valid."
